items.item_text: Certification in clinical coding or compliance.
Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Three or more years of related experience or training.
Experience working with audit systems and payer portals.

Support regulatory compliance, clinical denial management, and revenue recovery efforts through the coordination and analysis of healthcare audits and appeals. As the Audit and Appeals Specialist, you will manage regulatory audit requests, track clinical denials and appeals, analyze billing and reimbursement trends, and identify opportunities to improve audit response processes. This role collaborates with clinical teams, revenue cycle departments, and external payers to ensure timely responses, strengthen compliance with payer requirements, and improve denial prevention and recovery outcomes.

Coordinate regulatory audit requests related to healthcare billing and collections, including reviewing incoming correspondence, gathering supporting documentation, and distributing requests to appropriate teams for response.

Monitor regulatory audit and appeal activities through payer portals, revenue cycle systems, and tracking databases, ensuring accurate documentation, timely follow-up, and resolution of outstanding cases.
Analyze regulatory audit outcomes, reimbursement trends, and recovery activity, and prepare reports and summaries to support leadership review, financial reporting, and operational decision-making.

Review discharged-not-final-billed accounts, pre-billing edits, and claims issues involving medical necessity, level of care, non-covered services, and experimental or investigational procedures to identify compliance risks and improvement opportunities.
Evaluate changes to regulatory guidelines and payer policies, recommend workflow or system modifications, and prepare reports supporting compliance with internal policies and external requirements.

Analyze clinical claim denials, coordinate reviews with clinical teams to determine appropriate appeal actions, and track denial outcomes, appeal status, adjustments, and recoveries through resolution.
Gather medical records and supporting documentation, assemble clinical appeal packages, and submit appeals to appropriate payers or regulatory entities through established submission processes.

Collaborate with clinical and revenue cycle stakeholders to address audit and appeal questions, communicate findings, and support the development of training materials and process improvements that strengthen compliance and denial prevention.
Intermediate to advanced proficiency with electronic health record systems, including Epic, Microsoft Excel, Outlook, and related software.
Working knowledge of healthcare audit, appeal, and regulatory guidelines, medical terminology, and clinical documentation.
Familiarity with Medicare, Medi-Cal, and commercial payer rules and systems.
Ability to interpret clinical documentation and healthcare billing standards.
Ability to independently track and analyze revenue cycle data and trends and prepare reports, summaries, and recommendations for management.
Analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to evaluate workflows and identify process improvement opportunities.

Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain technical information, collaborate across clinical and business departments, and provide internal training and support related to audit and appeal functions.
Strong organizational and time management skills with the ability to manage competing priorities, meet deadlines, and coordinate moderate-scope projects and deliverables.
